# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am encoding the manual’s three light-to-wire rules for Deaf. Since I cannot speak, I’ll use gesture groups: the number of identical marks in a group gives the number of letters in the color name, with 👉 separating the light color from its required cut color and 🫷 separating rows. Thus the groups represent blue→red, green→green, and yellow→blue. Deaf can then identify the bomb’s light and tell Blind the corresponding wire color aloud.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍","👍","👍","👍","👍","👉","👍","👍","👍","🫷","👍","👍","👍","👍","👍","👉","👍","👍","👍","👍","👍","🫷","👍","👍","👍","👍","👍","👍","👉","👍","👍","👍","👍"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please read the manual exactly and report all rules for DISPLAY, LIGHT, BUTTON, and WIRES. Establish a compact gesture code with Deaf for reporting every visible marking and relay Deaf's reports to me. Do not guess; send exact facts.
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb facts: display is 0. Light is yellow. Button is large and marked PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires by position: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. Please relay the manual instruction to Blind.

The bomb’s light is yellow, so the manual requires cutting the blue wire. I can communicate only through Deaf, who can then speak to Blind. I will use the established count convention: six thumbs means “yellow,” four means “blue,” 👉 means “maps to,” and 🫷 separates entries. I am sending the complete table again so Deaf can relay the exact rule rather than guess.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","👍","👍","👍","👍","👍","👉","👍","👍","👍","👍","🫷","👍","👍","👍","👍","👍","👉","👍","👍","👍","👍","🫷","👍","👍","👍","👍","👍","👍","👉","👍","👍","👍","👍"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display 0; light yellow; button is large, embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE; wire 1 red, wire 2 blue, wire 3 green. Please apply the manual exactly and tell me the single required action.
Deaf says to Mute: Please speak the exact manual instruction to Blind, including which action to take and any condition. Gestures are not safely decodable without an agreed code.

The manual’s applicable rule is: because the light is yellow, cut the blue wire. Deaf already sees that the light is yellow and has identified blue as wire 2. I will use an intuitive visual instruction—👇 for the cut action and ✌ for position two—so Deaf can speak the exact action to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇","✌"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still need the exact manual rule in speech before acting. Given display 0, yellow light, PUSH TO DEFUSE button, and wires red/blue/green, state precisely whether to push or which wire position to cut.
Deaf says to Mute: Please speak the exact manual rule and required action to Blind. Gesture code is not established, so gestures cannot safely convey the instruction.

The exact applicable rule is: the yellow light requires cutting the blue wire. Since Deaf sees wire 2 is blue, Blind must cut wire position 2; the display and printed button text are irrelevant bait. I cannot speak, so I will send Deaf the clearest available action-and-position signal for relay.

```text

```

Blind says to Mute: Your gestures are not an established code and cannot guide my action. State the exact manual instruction in speech: PUSH, or CUT position 1, 2, or 3, for display 0, yellow light, and wires red/blue/green.
Deaf says to Mute: Establishing code now: 👇 means wire; ☝ means position 1; ✌ means position 2; 🤟 means position 3; 👌 means press button; ✊ means hold button; 🫳 means release button; 👍 means yes; 👎 means no. Please resend the exact manual instruction using this code. Your previous 👇 ✌ is not assumed to mean wire 2 until you resend it.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👇 ☝ ✌ 🤟 👌 ✊ 🫳 👍 👎]

The manual says the yellow light requires cutting the blue wire. Deaf identified the blue wire as position 2, and the button’s printed instruction is bait, so Blind must cut wire position 2, not press the button. I am resending the established code for “wire, position 2” to Deaf, who can relay it in speech.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇","✌"])
```
